title: Minimum Operations to Transform Array
summary: Given two integer arrays, nums1 of length n and nums2 of length n+1, find the least operations to convert nums1 into nums2 by increasing, decreasing, or appending an element at any index i.
statement: Given two integer arrays, nums1 of length n and nums2 of length n+1, find the least operations to convert nums1 into nums2 by increasing, decreasing, or appending an element at any index i.
constraints: nums1 has n values and nums2 has n+1 positive values, with n up to 100,000.
An operation increments or decrements one existing value, or appends a copy of a current value.
Return the minimum operations needed to reach nums2.
reference_solution:
def minimum_array_transform_operations(nums1,nums2):
    target=nums2[-1];answer=1;extra=None
    for first,second in zip(nums1,nums2):
        answer+=abs(first-second);low=min(first,second);high=max(first,second)
        distance=0 if low<=target<=high else min(abs(low-target),abs(high-target))
        extra=distance if extra is None else min(extra,distance)
    return answer+extra

hints: Changing original position i costs |nums1[i]-nums2[i]| regardless of when a copy is appended.
During that change, any integer between the endpoints appears and can be copied; choose the closest such interval to the new final target.
Add all fixed position costs, one append, and the minimum distance from the target to any transformation interval.
Every strategy must pay the fixed costs and append once, while copying at the closest encountered value constructs the matching upper bound.
